newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senator sees tax amnesty getting $275 million.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senator sees tax amnesty getting $275 million.

text.p: New York State Senator Emanuel Gold, D-Queens, who said the state's tax amnesty program could collect up to $275 million, on Monday recommended that the funds go to school districts to help cut property taxes.

The state senator's forecast was much more optimistic than the official forecast. In its 1997 fiscal budget, New York State projected that it would collect about $110 million from its second tax amnesty program, which ended on January 31.

Jack McPadden, a spokesman for Gold, the ranking Democrat on the Senate finance committee, said that the senator's estimate was based on how much cash the state had counted as of late last week. The total could rise substantially once all the tax returns have been opened because filers typically wait until the last minute.

"My information was as of Thursday morning, the 30th, they had, I believe the number was about $124 million that already was in the bank...The past history is that the money that comes in in the final week is probably 70 to 80 percent of the money raised," McPadden said, adding a large volume of returns have yet to be processed.

A spokesman for the state tax department, who earlier said that New York State had taken in $51 million in the first two months of the program, which began on November 1, could not immediately comment on the state senator's estimate. A 1986 tax amnesty program netted the state about $400 million.

The state senator urged that the windfall be used to pay about $190 million that New York State owes school districts, saying it was the high cost of local taxes, not state taxes, that give the state a reputation for being a high-tax state. "Using this money to honor commitments for school aid would bring credibility to our promise to offer property tax relief and would allow for immediate relief," Gold said, in prepared remarks.
He also saluted Republican Gov George Pataki's efforts to help reduce property taxes.
